item.title: Taiwan utility expands green power sales as firms seek renewable supply
item.description: New short-term and one-year products aim to help companies meet ESG and supply-chain requirements.

item.title: The ocean has finally entered the global climate debate
item.description: The world has started to recognise that the climate’s fate depends on what happens to the ocean. At COP30, ocean-based solutions attracted significant attention and investment, but much more must be done to establish the governance structures required for safeguarding this critical planetary system.

item.title: Floating solar has large-scale renewable potential in Malaysia, but challenges remain
item.description: Though not the most widely deployed solution, floating solar farms bypass land and social constraints, making efficient use of available space to help achieve Malaysia’s renewable energy target.

item.title: The ESG skills gap nobody’s talking about
item.description: Many of the people expected to deliver on increasing sustainability requirements don’t even work in ESG – and there is a shortage of people who can bridge the gap between purpose and performance.

item.title: Cebu landfill collapse underscores Philippines’ failed waste management system, say environmentalists
item.description: Dozens of waste workers remain missing following an avalanche of garbage at a landfill site in the central Philippines that occurred on 8 January.

item.title: Jeffrey Sachs: China is unequivocally the world's climate power today. Asean's opportunity is next.
item.description: The economist and president of the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network explained to the Eco-Business Podcast how China’s green industrial and financial capabilities can help accelerate Southeast Asia's transition to net zero.

item.title: China’s clean tech charm offensive wins Global South hearts and minds
item.description: A new survey shows growing public willingness to buy Chinese clean technologies.

item.title: South Korea to scale up livestock waste fuel to boost renewables by 2030
item.description: The agriculture ministry says manure-based solid fuel could power 38,000 homes annually by 2030.

item.title: Q&A: What Trump’s US exit from UNFCCC and IPCC could mean for climate action
item.description: The Trump administration in the US has announced its intention to withdraw from the UN’s landmark climate treaty, alongside 65 other international bodies that “no longer serve American interests”.

item.title: How the Global South tried to steer the recent UN Environment Assembly
item.description: Despite pushback, Global South delegates achieved consensus on a number of issues and an increased budget for the UN Environment Programme.
